resolved_findings.title: Same-origin crossing kernels cannot have negative products
resolved_findings.evidence: For K_b(x,v)=1{x+vt<z}-1{x<0}, x>=0 implies K_b>=0 for every b; x<0 implies K_b<=0 for every b. Consequently K_b K_c>=0 pointwise. The text asserts the opposite. Oppositely oriented intervals from the same origin are disjoint up to endpoints.
resolved_findings.requested_repair: Correct the explanation. Differently based increments can have negative covariance, but not this pair of same-origin kernels. Preserve the correct polarization formula and the pseudometric qualification.
resolved_findings.resolution: Reread corrected same-origin sign explanation and increment qualification.

resolved_findings.title: Close the simultaneous finite-crossing argument for uncountably many segments
resolved_findings.evidence: Finite Poisson count for each deterministic segment does not by itself produce one probability-one event on which every segment has finite crossings. The asserted admissibility is correct under the stated moment condition, but the needed simultaneous step is absent.
resolved_findings.requested_repair: Give the short compact-window estimate: every trajectory meeting [-R,R] x [-T,T] has |x|<=R+T|v|; the envelope intensity is integral (2R+2T|v|) dnu<infinity. Intersect these probability-one finiteness events over positive integer R,T. This also gives spatial local finiteness and finite crossings for every bounded segment on a single event.
resolved_findings.resolution: Reread the full proof. A trajectory meeting [-R,R] x [-T,T] necessarily has |x|<=R+T|v|. The resulting envelope has finite intensity integral (2R+2T|v|) dnu under the stated moment condition. Intersecting its finite-count events over positive integer R,T yields one probability-one event covering every bounded spacetime window and hence every bounded segment and spatial window at every time. This closes the uncountable-segment quantifier gap.

resolved_findings.title: Establish the nonnegative expectation identity before using it to extend the proof
resolved_findings.evidence: Only simple-function expectations have been proved when the proof invokes E N|f_n-f|=mu|f_n-f| for a general integrand. The covariance extension is otherwise sound.
resolved_findings.requested_repair: Insert a monotone-simple-approximation step for every nonnegative measurable h, using canonical monotone convergence (0A7A), to establish E Nh=mu h. Then L1 integrability gives almost-sure absolute convergence of Nf and validates the stated L1/L2 approximation argument.
resolved_findings.resolution: Reread the full proof and canonical 0A7A. Sigma-finiteness permits increasing nonnegative simple approximants with finite-measure support. Monotone convergence for integration against the random counting measure, expectation, and the intensity measure establishes E N h=mu h for all nonnegative measurable h, including infinite values, before it is used for L1 differences. E N|f|<infinity then gives almost-sure absolute convergence. The subsequent L1 and L2 covariance approximation is noncircular.

resolved_findings.title: Distinguish velocity flux from normalized mean velocity
resolved_findings.evidence: The weights rho_1=1/5 and rho_2=1/10 sum to 3/10, not one. The displayed 1/5 is sum rho_i V_i, a flux, not a mean velocity.
resolved_findings.requested_repair: Replace 'weighted mean velocity' by 'flux', or divide by rho_1+rho_2 and state the mean velocity is 2/3.
resolved_findings.resolution: Reread the entire example. The displayed sum rho_i V_i=1/5 is now explicitly the velocity-label flux; division by rho_1+rho_2=3/10 gives the normalized mean velocity 2/3. The density and effective-speed arithmetic remain correct.

resolved_findings.title: Strict rank fails for permanently coincident free trajectories
resolved_findings.evidence: 4C05 permits touching rods. For a=1, initial left endpoints (0,1), and both velocities zero, contraction gives x_1=x_2=0. The strict-left count R_i(t) in 4C06 is zero for both labels at every time, so both reconstructed left endpoints are zero rather than 0 and 1. Taking right limits does not resolve a permanent tie.
resolved_findings.requested_repair: Either define rank using a fixed tie order for permanently identical free trajectories (and right-limit ordering for transient crossings), or explicitly restrict 4C06 to pairwise distinct initial free positions. Preserve the general sorted construction in 4C05 and update packet proof scope if the contract is restricted.
resolved_findings.resolution: Reread both complete pages. Rank now counts lexicographically by (free position, velocity, fixed label). Velocity order at a transient tie is the right-time order; fixed labels resolve permanently identical trajectories. This is a total order with distinct ranks 0,...,N-1, so adding a times the rank preserves the sorted rod configuration, including touching rods. For a=1, x_1=x_2=0 and v_1=v_2=0, the ranks are 0 and 1 and the endpoints are 0 and 1. Isolated binary crossings have shifts +/-a; multiple collisions use the full rank change rather than a falsely universal binary shift.
